title: 'Tis God the Spirit Leads
description: 'Tis God the Spirit Leads in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 510 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Way of God with the Spirit”, where the book credits them to the Christian Psalmist.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: 'Tis God the spir-it leads In paths be-fore un-known: The work to be per-formed is ours; The strength is all his own.

lines: The work to be performed is ours;
The strength is all his own.
And hope at last to reach the prize,
His is the power by which we act,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
